articles.title: Rajadas de vento de até 96 km/h derrubam árvores em Piracicaba | G1
articles.standfirst: Temporal deste sábado (7) provocou quedas de árvores em diversos bairros, deixou imóveis sem energia elétrica e danificou parte da cobertura do Terminal da Pauliceia.
articles.summary: Temporal deste sábado (7) provocou quedas de árvores em diversos bairros, deixou imóveis sem energia elétrica e danificou parte da cobertura do Terminal da Pauliceia.
articles.body:
A chuva acompanhada de rajadas de vento de até 96,1 km/h que atingiu Piracicaba (SP) na tarde deste sábado (7) derrubou ao menos 19 árvores e galhos em diferentes regiões da cidade, provocou falta de energia elétrica e causou danos à estrutura do Terminal de Ônibus Urbano da Pauliceia .

Segundo a Defesa Civil do Estado de São Paulo, uma estação do Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) em Piracicaba registrou rajadas de vento de até 96,1 km/h às 16h.

De acordo com balanço parcial divulgado pela prefeitura, as ocorrências de queda de árvores e galhos foram registradas em bairros como Tupi, Nova Piracicaba, Jupiá, Nova América, Jardim São Jorge, Higienópolis, Terras do Engenho, São Dimas, Centro, Jardim Elite e Dois Córregos .

As equipes municipais foram mobilizadas para a retirada de árvores caídas, desobstrução de vias e atendimento de situações que oferecem risco à população.

Os trabalhos são coordenados pelo Comitê Municipal de Gestão de Crise Climática, em conjunto com o Corpo de Bombeiros e a CPFL.

Rajadas de até 96 km/h derrubam árvores e danificam estruturas em Piracicaba — Foto: Arquivo pessoal/Gleison Santos/Michele Fernanda

Na região da Pauliceia, parte do telhado do Terminal de Ônibus Urbano foi danificada pela força do temporal.

O espaço permanece parcialmente interditado, mas segue funcionando normalmente, segundo a administração municipal.

A chuva também provocou interrupções no fornecimento de energia elétrica na Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA) Vila Cristina e em bairros como Castelinho, Santa Rosa, Jupiá e Centro.

Já na comunidade Pereirinha, uma residência sofreu danos em sua estrutura. A Prefeitura informou que fará o atendimento à família para oferecer o suporte necessário.

articles.title: Resgate de paciente com epilepsia no Amazonas após 48h de crises | G1
articles.standfirst: Mulher foi transportada de avião para Manaus após agravamento do quadro de saúde. A viagem até a capital levou menos de meia hora.
articles.summary: Resgate de paciente com epilepsia no Amazonas mobilizou transporte aéreo após 48 horas de crises convulsivas em área ribeirinha de difícil acesso.
articles.body:
Paciente com epilepsia é resgatada após 48 horas de convulsões em comunidade ribeirinha no AM — Foto: Victor Levy/SSP-AM

Uma mulher com epilepsia, que não teve a identidade divulgada, foi resgatada de avião após passar 48 horas com crises convulsivas em uma comunidade ribeirinha de Manaus . O resgate ocorreu na sexta-feira (6), no Assentamento Nazaré, na Costa do Tabocal, a cerca de 80 quilômetros da área urbana da capital.

A paciente faz tratamento em Manaus e havia sido internada recentemente. No entanto, começou a apresentar crises sucessivas após uma troca de medicamento. Com o agravamento do quadro, foi necessário realizar o transporte aeromédico.

O resgate foi feito pelo Departamento Integrado de Operações Aéreas (Dioa), da Secretaria de Estado de Segurança Pública do Amazonas (SSP-AM), com apoio de uma médica do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu).

Segundo a médica intervencionista Alessandra Said, a paciente tem epilepsia de difícil controle e precisava de atendimento rápido.

"Conseguimos fazer esse voo da melhor maneira possível, com toda a segurança. Assim, conseguimos resgatar essa paciente e trouxemos ela em total segurança. Agora, a paciente pode ser levada já mais estabilizada até o nosso ponto de suporte daqui de Manaus", explicou a médica.

De acordo com o coordenador do Dioa, delegado Rafael Montenegro, o deslocamento de avião reduziu o tempo de transporte de cerca de cinco a seis horas para menos de meia hora .

"Um resgate que demoraria, em média, por volta de cinco a seis horas, o departamento aéreo demorou 22 minutos para ir e 25 minutos para voltar. A paciente já foi encaminhada para uma unidade hospitalar, o Hospital 28 de Agosto", afirmou.

articles.title: Who is behind Europe’s suspected hybrid attacks?
articles.summary: Bomb hoaxes and supermarket cyberattacks are heightening security fears.
articles.body:
Italy says civilian infrastructure in Europe is “under attack”.

A series of bomb threats this week grounded flights and put airports on high alert. No explosives were found, and the threats appear to be false.

But the disruption is not limited to aviation. Hackers have also targeted supermarket freezers in several countries, raising temperatures and spoiling food.

Together, the incidents are raising fears and questions about a wider campaign of hybrid attacks.

Who could be behind these threats? Are they connected? And can European nations come together to counter these acts of aggression?

articles.title: Bombeiros levam carro para oficina após cobra de 1,5 metro se esconder entre tanque de combustível e assoalho em MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Como o acesso ao animal era difícil, os bombeiros levaram o veículo a uma oficina para rebaixar o tanque de combustível e conseguir fazer a captura. Ocorrência foi registrada em Januária, nesta sexta-feira (6).
articles.summary: Como o acesso ao animal era difícil, os bombeiros levaram o veículo a uma oficina para rebaixar o tanque de combustível e conseguir fazer a captura. Ocorrência foi registrada em Januária, nesta sexta-feira (6).
articles.body:
Cobra se escondeu o tanque de combustível e o assoalho do carro — Foto: Corpo de Bombeiros/Divulgação

Uma cobra da espécie cipó-marrom foi capturada pelo Corpo de Bombeiros após se esconder em um carro estacionado na garagem de uma casa em Januária , no Norte de Minas.

Os militares foram acionados depois que os moradores perceberam que a serpente havia entrado embaixo do veículo e não conseguiram mais visualizá-la.

Durante a vistoria, a equipe utilizou uma almofada pneumática para elevar o automóvel e identificar que o animal estava escondido entre o tanque de combustível e o assoalho.

Segundo os bombeiros, como o acesso era difícil, foi necessário encaminhar o carro a uma oficina, onde o tanque de combustível foi rebaixado para permitir a retirada da serpente.

Com técnicas de manejo e equipamentos adequados, os militares conseguiram capturar o animal com segurança.

Após a captura, a serpente, que media cerca de 1,5 metro, foi transportada e solta em uma área afastada do perímetro urbano, em seu habitat natural.

Esta foi a segunda captura de uma cobra da mesma espécie realizada pelos bombeiros em Januária nesta semana. Na segunda-feira (2), os militares resgataram um animal de aproximadamente um metro que estava escondido dentro de um vaso de planta , no quintal de uma casa, no bairro Alto dos Poções.

articles.title: Eleições EUA 2028: Como as midterms impactam a sucessão de Trump | G1
articles.standfirst: A expectativa em torno da eleição presidencial já começou — e aqui estão algumas pistas que as 'midterms' deram do que pode acontecer.
articles.summary: A expectativa em torno da eleição presidencial já começou — e aqui estão algumas pistas que as 'midterms' deram do que pode acontecer.
articles.body:
Votos da eleição de meio de mandato nos Estados Unidos ainda estão sendo contados, mas o cenário político já se volta para a corrida presidencial de 2028.

Impulsionados por vitórias significativas no Congresso, os democratas ganharam força enquanto se preparam para a disputa pela sucessão do presidente Donald Trump .

Mas um bom desempenho nas eleições de meio de mandato, as midterms , não garante a conquista da Casa Branca dois anos depois. O democrata Barack Obama foi reeleito em 2012, apesar de grandes vitórias republicanas em 2010.

Não há oficialmente candidatos para suceder Trump, mas nomes em potencial estão se preparando nos bastidores.

Declarações do vice-presidente J.D. Vance com reflexões sobre as derrotas dos republicanos nas midterms foram interpretadas como uma preparação para uma candidatura em 2028.

Os resultados da eleição da última terça-feira e a magnitude histórica dos ganhos democratas podem moldar a corrida pela Casa Branca de diversas maneiras. Aqui estão quatro pontos observados nas midterms que dão pistas sobre como poderá ser a próxima corrida presidencial americana.

1. Os grandes vencedores das midterms agora têm um impulso

Vários candidatos em potencial para a presidência concorreram nas midterms , e alguns deles se destacaram.

O senador democrata da Geórgia Jon Ossoff venceu com uma margem considerável no Estado, onde Trump ganhou em 2024.

Embora já tenha afirmado que não pretende se candidatar à presidência, sua campanha bem-sucedida, com diversas viralizações na internet, projetou Ossoff nacionalmente.

Outro potencial candidato democrata, o governador da Pensilvânia Josh Shapiro , derrotou com folga seu adversário republicano.

Shapiro não se comprometeu com uma candidatura em 2028, mas analistas apontam para sua ampla popularidade na Pensilvânia, um dos Estados-chave nas eleições, como um sinal de que ele poderia ser competitivo nacionalmente.

O governador de Illinois, JB Pritzker , também venceu após uma campanha que analistas de seu Estado descreveram como um "aquecimento" para uma candidatura presidencial.

O governador da Califórnia, Gavin Newsom , não pôde concorrer à reeleição nas eleições de meio de mandato, mas está interessado no resultado de uma iniciativa popular para taxar bilionários — contra a qual ele fez campanha por considerar que a mudança poderia afugentar os ricos e levar a perdas de arrecadação no Estado.

Pelo lado republicano, houve dois nomes com potencial para concorrer em 2028 no Arkansas.

O senador republicano Tom Cotton e a governadora Sarah Huckabee Sanders — ex-secretária de imprensa do governo Trump — conseguiram se manter no cargo por uma margem menor do que antes, ambos conquistando pouco mais da metade dos votos no Estado conservador.

2. JD Vance e aliados de Trump sob pressão

As pesquisas de boca de urna sugerem que a maré negativa para os republicanos se deveu em parte à raiva sentida pelos eleitores em relação às ações do governo Trump.

Isso pode representar um desafio para seus potenciais sucessores que fazem parte do gabinete presidencial, incluindo o vice-presidente, JD Vance, e o secretário de Estado, Marco Rubio .

"A única pessoa que foi gravemente prejudicada por esta campanha eleitoral foi Vance", analisa Karen Beckwith, professora de ciência política na Case Western Reserve University, em Ohio.

Vance já procurou se distanciar da derrota — e de uma aventura de política externa no Irã que foi politicamente desastrosa para o seu partido.

"O motivo da nossa derrota foi a guerra", escreveu ele na rede social X.

Rubio negou os rumores de que estaria considerando deixar o cargo para concorrer à presidência em 2028.

Mas outros possíveis candidatos republicanos podem se beneficiar por não fazerem parte do governo. Alguns já vêm se posicionando sobre o que deu errado e quais são os próximos passos.

Numa longa publicação no X, o senador Ted Cruz , que não concorreu à reeleição este ano, afirmou que muitos políticos republicanos parecem "não se importar" com os problemas econômicos enfrentados pelos eleitores.

"Está escuro agora, mas sempre é mais escuro antes do amanhecer, e a manhã está chegando", escreveu ele. "Essa é a minha oração fervorosa e esse é o meu compromisso com vocês."

O governador da Flórida, Ron DeSantis , que abandonou sua candidatura presidencial em 2024 dias antes das primárias republicanas em que enfrentaria Trump, também se mostrou crítico. Ele destacou as vitórias de seu partido na Flórida como um sinal do que pode ser alcançado.

3. Democratas de esquerda e de centro de olho no futuro

Tanto a ala centrista quanto a ala de esquerda do Partido Democrata reivindicaram a vitória com os resultados das midterms , enquanto cada lado analisa seus possíveis candidatos para 2028.

Dezenas de pessoas já estão se mobilizando para 2028, disse Jim Messina, ex-conselheiro de Obama, à BBC.

A vitória de El-Sayed em Michigan foi um momento decisivo para os democratas de esquerda, pois ele triunfou em um Estado-pêndulo.

Seus apoiadores agora afirmam que sua vitória pode impulsionar candidatos de esquerda nas eleições de 2028.

"As antigas noções de elegibilidade ficaram para trás, e economistas populistas ousados, de fora do sistema, provaram que podem vencer em Estados decisivos", disse Adam Green, cofundador do Comitê de Campanha para Mudanças Progressistas.

Green acrescenta que "o cenário está favorável" para candidatos como a representante democrata de Nova York Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez concorrerem nas primárias.

Democratas moderados também reivindicaram vitórias em todo o país. O " Blue Dog Caucus ", grupo de democratas moderados e conservadores, conquistaram pelo menos 14 cadeiras no Congresso, quase dobrando seu tamanho atual.

Isso levou muitos dentro desse segmento do partido a defender que candidatos de centro que se apresentam como pragmáticos e dispostos a trabalhar com conservadores poderiam atrair eleitores republicanos.

Dado o sucesso dos candidatos democratas que focaram em questões relacionadas ao custo de vida, é provável que uma abordagem que priorize a economia volte a ser um foco daqui a dois anos.

Amirah Siquierah, diretora de assuntos federais do Partido das Famílias Trabalhadoras, afirmou que os candidatos vitoriosos em 2028 combinarão o populismo econômico com novas preocupações, como com os data centers (grandes centros de processamento de dados que permitem o funcionamento da internet e de serviços digitais).

Ambos os partidos terão de lidar com um cenário político em transformação e uma coligação de apoio instável para 2028.

Regiões do país antes consideradas "seguras" para os republicanos não podem mais ser vistas como redutos conservadores.

O Texas agora conta com apenas um candidato republicano em nível estadual, o que significa que seus 40 votos no colégio eleitoral podem estar em disputa em 2028.

Christina Pascucci, analista política e ex-candidata ao Senado pela Califórnia, afirmou que as eleições de meio de mandato "desafiaram pressupostos políticos antigos" e mostraram que "nenhum dos partidos pode se dar ao luxo de considerar seus redutos tradicionais como garantidos".

Isso vale tanto para democratas quanto para republicanos, que precisarão conquistar os eleitores indecisos, acrescenta Pascucci, diretora-executiva da consultoria Atlas Global.

"Nenhum dos partidos é dono desses eleitores", resume.

Os eleitores latinos e da classe trabalhadora que apoiaram Trump deram um passo atrás, revertendo muitos dos ganhos que ele havia obtido com esses eleitorados em sua bem-sucedida campanha de 2024.

Driena Sixto, ex-porta-voz da organização Turning Point USA e comentarista política conservadora, diz à BBC acreditar que os republicanos terão que mudar sua mensagem para os eleitores latinos antes de 2028.

"Da última vez, a mensagem da campanha foi sobre comunidades seguras e o combate ao tráfico de pessoas", disse ela.

"Depois que o presidente tomou posse, acho que muitas das mensagens da Casa Branca deram muita ênfase às deportações. Essa foi a causa da divisão."

articles.title: 'Window for military action narrowing': Trump urged to launch new campaign against Iran before January
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump's advisers have urged him to launch fresh military strikes against Iran before a new Democratic-controlled Congress takes office
articles.body: US President Donald Trump's advisers have urged him to launch fresh military strikes against Iran before a new Democratic-controlled Congress takes office in January, warning that the window for military action could narrow once lawmakers return to Washington, according to a report by NBC News.Citing two US officials, NBC News reported that administration and defence officials had told Trump that a new Congress could complicate any military campaign through investigations, restrictions on funding or resolutions seeking to block further strikes. Some advisers have therefore pushed for renewed military action before January, although the president has yet to make a decision.Trump received an updated briefing on Thursday on the Iranian threat and the military options available to Washington. The meeting was attended by Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Joint Chiefs of Staff Chairman General Dan Caine. According to the report, Hegseth has continued to advocate renewed strikes, while other members of the administration have cautioned that further escalation could derail diplomatic efforts.Vice President JD Vance, meanwhile, has been pursuing negotiations with Tehran in an attempt to prevent another round of conflict. A fresh military campaign, if authorised, could be shorter but more intense than previous operations, with Iran's oil and gas infrastructure and nuclear facilities, including the Pickaxe Mountain site, among the potential targets discussed with Trump.A White House official told NBC News that Trump had "all options available at any time", adding that only the president knew what he would do and when.The push for a military decision comes amid parallel diplomatic efforts to prevent tensions from escalating further. Qatar has been mediating between Washington and Tehran, with two Middle East government officials telling the Associated Press that Iran was reviewing proposals from Doha aimed at resolving differences over its nuclear programme.Trump also spoke to Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al-Thani on Friday about efforts to de-escalate tensions and secure a comprehensive agreement. The Qatari leader emphasised dialogue and diplomatic solutions, warning against further escalation and stressing the importance of protecting maritime navigation and energy supplies.Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi has also held telephone conversations with regional counterparts, including officials from Iraq and Tunisia, to discuss diplomatic efforts. articles.title: 'A soulful rendition’: Rajnath Singh shares video of IAF warriors' patriotic melody
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday shared a video of Indian Air Force (IAF) personnel singing a patriotic song, praising their musical
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Saturday shared a video of Indian Air Force (IAF) personnel singing a patriotic song, praising their musical talent and saying their performance reflected the passion and dedication with which they serve the country.In the clip, which is shared on X, showed two uniformed IAF air warriors singing together in a large hall.The personnel sang lines including "Jeene ki ijazat de de ya hukm shahadat de de" and "O des mere" in the 45-second video.Sharing the video, Rajnath Singh described the performance as a "soulful rendition" and praised the air warriors for bringing the same commitment to music that they demonstrate in their service."A soulful rendition by our talented IAF Air Warriors! Their voices reflect the same passion, pride and dedication that define their service to the nation. Truly a treat to listen to!" he wrote on X.Earlier, Rajnath Singh urged the armed forces to remain on the highest alert to deal with emerging threats to India's national security, warning that adversaries could use misinformation and social media to target both soldiers and local residents.Addressing air warriors at the Bagdogra Air Force Station in West Bengal, near the frontier with China in the eastern sector, Singh said the nature of security threats was changing and that the military needed to prepare for challenges beyond conventional warfare.Without naming any country, he said adversaries were increasingly looking to exploit weaknesses rather than engage in direct military confrontation."Often, the adversary avoids direct confrontation and instead seeks to exploit our vulnerabilities. Through social media, the adversary may attempt to sow doubt in the minds of the local population and our soldiers by spreading misleading information," he said."In such a scenario, your role extends beyond that of an ordinary soldier," he added.According to the Defence Ministry, Singh called for the armed forces to maintain the highest level of operational readiness, with particular attention to domain awareness, cyber resilience and the reliability of information.He said modern warfare was no longer limited to conventional fighting along national borders. It now included asymmetric warfare, proxy conflicts, cyberattacks, drone swarms, information operations and attempts to shape public narratives.Singh described Bagdogra as a strategically important location and a key part of India's security framework, particularly for the North-Eastern region.He praised the personnel stationed there for their courage and commitment, saying their presence provided a strong defence shield for India's eastern sector. articles.title: 10 years of Juvenile Justice Act: Has the law helped children reform or pushed more towards adult trials?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Should a child accused of a crime be punished like an adult, or given an opportunity to reform?
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Should a child accused of a crime be punished like an adult, or given an opportunity to reform? India's Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, is built around the principle that children in conflict with the law deserve a chance to change and reintegrate into society. Yet, it makes an exception for those aged 16–18 accused of heinous offences, allowing them to be considered for trial as adults.A decade after the law came into force, however, questions remain about how effectively it has delivered on its promise. Are children receiving the care, education and rehabilitation they are entitled to? Are juvenile homes equipped to help them rebuild their lives? And how well do the safeguards work when a child faces the prospect of an adult trial?Here is what the law provides, how the system is meant to function and where implementation continues to fall short.Key changes under the 2015 ActThe 2015 Act brought significant changes to India's juvenile justice framework, most notably by classifying offences into three categories: petty, serious and heinous. Section 2(33) defines heinous offences as those carrying a minimum punishment of seven years or more.“The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 introduced several significant changes to the juvenile justice framework. It classified offences into three categories, which are petty, serious and heinous offences, with heinous offences defined under Section 2(33) as offences carrying a minimum punishment of seven years or more,” said senior advocate Vivek Narayan Sharma.Another major change was the introduction of a preliminary assessment under Section 15. It allows the Juvenile Justice Board (JJB) to examine whether children aged 16–18 accused of heinous offences should continue to be dealt with under the juvenile justice system or have their cases transferred to the Children's Court for trial as adults."The Act also brought adoption within its statutory framework and gave the Central Adoption Resource Authority (CARA) statutory status under Section 68. It strengthened non-institutional care through provisions for foster care, sponsorship and aftercare for young persons leaving childcare institutions under Section 46," Sharma said.Section 41 made registration compulsory for all Child Care Institutions (CCIs). The 2021 amendment further strengthened administrative oversight by expanding the District Magistrate's supervisory role over Child Welfare Committees (CWCs) and childcare institutions.“The 2021 Amendment introduced a separate category of serious offences carrying a maximum punishment of more than seven years but having no minimum sentence, and expanded the District Magistrate's oversight over Child Welfare Committees and Child Care Institutions,” Sharma said.The 16–18 adult trial provisionDoes being 16 or 17 automatically mean a child accused of murder or another heinous offence can be tried as an adult? No. Section 15 requires the JJB to assess the child's mental and physical capacity, ability to understand the consequences of the alleged offence and the circumstances in which it was committed.“The Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 introduced Section 15, which provides for a preliminary assessment of children aged 16–18 years accused of committing heinous offences to determine whether their cases should be retained by the Juvenile Justice Board or transferred to the Children's Court for trial as an adult,” Sharma said.The provision followed concerns that adults could exploit juveniles. Sharma represented Shilpa Arora Sharma in Shilpa Arora Sharma v Union of India.In Barun Chandra Thakur v Master Bholu (July 13, 2022), the Supreme Court said the delicate assessment requires expert help from psychologists or psycho-social workers where needed.In Shilpa Mittal v State (NCT of Delhi) (2020), the Supreme Court classified offences with a maximum sentence above seven years but no minimum as serious, not heinous. On July 21, 2026, in X v State of Bihar, it held murder under IPC Section 302/BNS Section 103(1) to be heinous because life imprisonment is its implied minimum.The preliminary assessment does not establish guilt. It only decides whether the case should remain before the JJB or go to the Children's Court.From apprehension to the JJB's decisionThe Act lays down safeguards from the moment a child comes into contact with the police.Under Section 10, the Special Juvenile Police Unit or a designated Child Welfare Police Officer must produce the child before the JJB within 24 hours of apprehension, excluding the time required for the journey. A child cannot be kept in a police lock-up or jail, handcuffed or subjected to intimidation. The child's parents or guardians must also be informed.Section 12 makes bail the general rule, even in cases involving non-bailable offences. Bail can be denied only if the child's release is likely to expose them to danger, bring them into contact with known criminals or defeat the ends of justice. The JJB must record its reasons for refusing bail.The child is also entitled to legal representation and free legal aid under Section 13. Parents or guardians and the probation officer must be informed, while the child must be made aware of the allegations. The law prohibits forcing a child to confess or sign a statement.Section 14 requires the JJB to conduct a child-friendly inquiry, hear the child and consider the social investigation report. The inquiry should ordinarily be completed within four months, with a possible extension of two months for recorded reasons.If the child is found to have committed the offence, Section 18 provides for rehabilitative measures such as counselling, community service, probation or placement in a special home.These safeguards are underpinned by the principles laid down in Section 3, which include the presumption of innocence, dignity and participation, the best interests of the child, privacy and confidentiality, non-discrimination, institutionalisation as a last resort, and rehabilitation and social reintegration.“The principles include presumption of innocence, right to dignity and participation, best interests of the child, privacy and confidentiality, non-discrimination and non-stigmatisation, institutionalisation as a measure of last resort, and rehabilitation and social reintegration,” Sharma said.JJBs and CWCs: Are the institutions functioning effectively?The juvenile justice system relies heavily on two statutory bodies. JJBs deal with children alleged to have committed offences, while CWCs are responsible for children in need of care and protection, including those who have been abandoned, abused or neglected.However, shortages of personnel and delays in filling vacancies have affected their functioning.In Sampurna Behura v Union of India (2018), the Supreme Court directed that vacancies in these bodies be filled within three months. The Delhi High Court subsequently set April 15, 2024, as the deadline for filling vacancies in CWCs and JJBs.The scale of the problem is reflected in the India Justice Report 2025. It found that 55% of cases before 362 JJBs were pending as of October 31, 2023. Around one in four boards lacked a full bench, while 30% of the responding boards lacked an attached legal services clinic.The report also highlighted the absence of a centralised public database to track the performance of these bodies, making it difficult to assess their functioning and identify gaps in service delivery.Juvenile homes: Is rehabilitation happening on the ground?The purpose of a juvenile home goes beyond keeping a child in custody. It is supposed to provide a safe environment, education, counselling and other support services that can help children return to society and rebuild their lives.But conditions in many institutions raise questions about whether this objective is being achieved.According to the India Justice Report, only 810 of the 1,992 mandated inspections were conducted across 166 homes in 14 states and one Union Territory. The report also found that 292 districts had just 40 homes exclusively for girls, alongside concerns about overcrowding and inadequate access to schooling.These shortcomings undermine the rehabilitative purpose of the law. A child placed in an institution should have access to education, healthcare, counselling and opportunities to develop skills, rather than simply being confined.The Act also provides for aftercare under Section 46, recognising that rehabilitation cannot end when a young person leaves an institution. Financial and other forms of assistance are intended to help them adjust to life outside and become independent.However, gaps in inspections, monitoring and institutional capacity make it difficult to establish how consistently these provisions are being implemented.Where does the system fall short, and what can be done?The Act provides several channels for addressing complaints about inadequate care or violations of children's rights. These include the CWC, District Child Protection Unit, District Magistrate and the State or National Commission for Protection of Child Rights. A writ petition can also be filed before the high court.Yet, the existence of legal safeguards does not necessarily translate into effective protection on the ground.Police, JJBs, CWCs and District Child Protection Units often operate in silos, weakening coordination and accountability. Vacancies, prolonged inquiries, limited access to legal aid and inadequate inspections further affect the system's ability to deliver timely and effective rehabilitation.The Juvenile Justice Act rests on an important premise: a child who commits an offence should not automatically be defined by that act for the rest of their life. Even where the law permits an adult trial, it requires an assessment and safeguards that recognise the child's age and capacity.Ten years on, the real measure of the Act's success will not simply be how many cases it processes or how many institutions it establishes. It will be whether children receive a fair hearing, meaningful rehabilitation, education and a genuine opportunity to rebuild their lives.

Bullying and trolling are not really the role of members of Congress. You are a public servant. Acquiring some skills is part of a healthy, balanced life. I recommend this to you. No need to be hateful all day!” Dhillon added.The social media exchange followed Dhillon's resignation as head of the Civil Rights Division, which Attorney General Todd Blanche announced on Thursday. Her approach drew criticism from Democrats and civil rights advocates, who argued that the department was moving away from its traditional responsibility of protecting civil rights.One major point of disagreement was the department's attempts to obtain voter registration data from states to examine potential non-citizen voting. Dhillon's division pursued legal action against states that did not provide the requested records and sent election monitors to polling locations.Dhillon's departure also followed a significant turnover among career staff at the Civil Rights Division. articles.title: A Florida landowner won $40,000 after a telecom company laid fibre cables outside an easement; the state's highest court has now ruled that an old legal-fees clause does not automatically bind later property owners
articles.summary: A property agreement can continue to affect land even after the original owners have sold it.
articles.body: A property agreement can continue to affect land even after the original owners have sold it. But do all the conditions in such an agreement automatically apply to future owners? The Florida Supreme Court has addressed this question in a dispute involving a telecommunications company that installed underground fibre-optic cables beyond an authorised easement. The property owner won $40,000 in trespass damages, but a separate dispute over legal fees eventually reached the state's highest court.In an opinion dated October 29, 2026, the Florida Supreme Court ruled that an agreement requiring the losing party to pay the winner's attorney fees does not automatically apply to future property owners. The ruling came in RJ's International Trading, LLC v. Crown Castle South, LLC, case number SC2024-0547, with the opinion available on Justia. The court answered a legal question referred by the US Court of Appeals for the Eleventh Circuit about when contractual obligations can pass to subsequent owners.How the dispute beganThe dispute dates back more than three decades, when Hidden Valley Corporation owned two neighbouring properties in Miami. It leased one property to BellSouth Mobility and allowed the telecommunications company to use part of the adjoining property for its operations. The arrangement was formalised through an easement agreement. An easement gives someone the legal right to use another person's property for a specific purpose without owning it. In this case, the agreement permitted the telecommunications company and its successors to use a defined portion of the neighbouring land.The agreement also stated that if either party filed a lawsuit to enforce its terms, the losing party would have to pay the successful party's reasonable attorney fees and court costs. Over the years, ownership of the properties changed hands. Eventually, RJ's International Trading LLC (RJI) acquired the property covered by the easement, while Crown Castle South LLC exercised rights under the agreement through a sublease from BellSouth.Fibre cables installed beyond the easementThe dispute arose in 2020, when Crown Castle excavated parts of RJI's property outside the authorised easement and installed underground fibre-optic cables. RJI filed a lawsuit in the US District Court for the Southern District of Florida, alleging trespass and breach of the easement agreement, among other claims.The district court found that Crown Castle had gone beyond the authorised boundaries. The case then proceeded to a six-day jury trial to determine damages. The jury awarded RJI $1 for breach of the easement agreement and $40,000 for trespass. It declined to award punitive damages.After the verdict, RJI sought additional attorney fees under the original agreement. It argued that the legal-fees clause was attached to the property and should therefore apply to later owners as well. However, the district court rejected the request, finding that the clause was not sufficiently connected to the property's use or enjoyment to automatically bind future owners.Why the legal-fees clause became importantRJI challenged the decision, taking the dispute to the Eleventh Circuit Court of Appeals. The appeals court sought clarification from the Florida Supreme Court on whether an attorney-fees clause in an easement agreement could automatically apply to people who acquired the property later. The Eleventh Circuit had separately considered whether RJI could claim the benefit of the provision as a party to the original agreement. However, that question was not part of the legal issue referred to the Florida Supreme Court. The central question was whether a contractual promise to pay legal expenses could become a permanent obligation attached to the land, even when a future owner had not signed the original agreement.The Florida Supreme Court explained that not every condition in a property agreement automatically applies to future owners. For an obligation to continue after a property is sold, it must have a direct connection to the land and its use or enjoyment. The court found that the attorney-fees clause did not meet this requirement. It dealt with who would pay legal expenses if a dispute went to court, rather than how the property could be used or maintained.How the court distinguished an earlier rulingThe justices also compared the dispute with Hayslip v. U.S. Home Corp., a 2022 Florida Supreme Court decision involving an arbitration clause in a property deed. In that earlier case, the court allowed the arbitration provision to apply to future owners because it concerned construction defects that could affect the condition of a home.The justices said the two situations were different. While construction-related arbitration could directly affect the property, an attorney-fees clause simply determines who pays legal costs after a dispute. It does not determine how the land is used or enjoyed. The court therefore ruled that the legal-fees provision could not automatically bind subsequent property owners.What happens next?The Florida Supreme Court answered the Eleventh Circuit's question in the negative and sent the matter back to the federal appeals court for further proceedings. The decision does not cancel RJI's earlier $40,000 trespass award. Instead, it clarifies that a legal-fees clause in an old property agreement does not automatically become an obligation for everyone who owns the land later.The ruling draws a distinction between conditions that directly concern a property's use and contractual terms that deal only with expenses arising from legal disputes.You use AI every day. articles.title: UK bride’s father was hospitalised with heart failure just days before her wedding; then she brought her wedding dress to his hospital room for a father-daughter dance
articles.summary: For Sinead Jackson, having her father walk her down the aisle was one of the moments she had looked forward to most at her wedding.
articles.body: For Sinead Jackson, having her father walk her down the aisle was one of the moments she had looked forward to most at her wedding. But just days before she was due to marry her partner, Stephen, her father, Leslie Healy, was admitted to hospital with a heart problem and was told he was too unwell to attend the ceremony.Rather than let the moment pass without him, Sinead found a way to share part of her wedding day with her father. She visited him at Tameside Hospital in England, wearing her wedding dress, and the two shared a father-daughter dance on the hospital's acute cardiology unit.According to a report by PEOPLE, Sinead, 36, was due to marry Stephen on October 10 in Hyde, England. Her father had been taken to Tameside Hospital after experiencing shortness of breath and heart palpitations. The report said doctors discovered he was in heart failure, leaving him unable to attend the wedding or walk his daughter down the aisle.The hospital confirmed that Leslie had been admitted to the acute cardiology unit shortly before the wedding. It said he was still undergoing investigations to establish the cause of his admission.Sinead wanted her father to see her in her wedding dressThe news was difficult for Sinead, who had been looking forward to her father seeing her dressed as a bride. Speaking to PEOPLE, she recalled how her mother called to tell her that Leslie had undergone a scan and needed to remain in hospital.When the family realised he would not be able to attend, she struggled to accept the change in plans. “I couldn’t stop crying,” she recalled. “It hit because it’s your dream, isn’t it? Having your dad there to walk you down the aisle. That’s the thing I was looking forward to most.”She also explained that her father had been waiting to see her in her wedding dress. “I waited weeks for Dad to see me in my dress because when I bought it, he said he wanted to see me wear it on the day. That was the dream, to see his first reaction,” she said.Sinead considered postponing the wedding, but Leslie encouraged her to go ahead. She told that she has four brothers and her father knew they would be there to support her. However, she was determined to see him before the ceremony. “My day couldn’t go ahead until I’d seen my dad,” she said.Hospital staff helped arrange the father-daughter danceAccording to the hospital's October 16 statement, staff on the acute cardiology unit learnt that Leslie would miss his daughter's wedding and arranged for Sinead to visit him in her wedding gown. Leslie was also dressed for the occasion. The visit gave the father and daughter an opportunity to share their first dance before the wedding ceremony, with Sinead's mother, Mary, other family members and hospital staff present.Sinead said that the moment moved everyone around them. “All the nurses and all the patients were crying,” she said. Leslie also spoke about the experience in the hospital's statement. “It was a very emotional day for us all, happiness for my daughter Sinead, as well as sadness at not being able to attend,” he said.Although Leslie could not be physically present at the ceremony, the family found another way to include him. Sinead's five-year-old son, Maxy, walked her down the aisle in his grandfather's place, at Leslie's request.An uncle also video-called Leslie from the wedding so he could watch his daughter walk down the aisle. According to PEOPLE, he followed the ceremony virtually from his hospital room. Sinead said seeing her father before the wedding helped her feel more relaxed.Sinead and Stephen have also planned to celebrate with Leslie and take wedding photographs together once he feels better. She said she intends to wear her wedding dress again while her father puts on his suit.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Did Abdul El-Sayed get his Wikipedia page edited to soften controversial sentences before Michigan Senate election? Larry Sanger responds
articles.summary: Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed's Wikipedia page was allegedly edited over several months to soften or remove references to controversies
articles.body: Michigan Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed's Wikipedia page was allegedly edited over several months to soften or remove references to controversies surrounding him ahead of the November 3 election, according to an investigation by researchers who tracked changes to the online encyclopedia.The edits were reportedly made by an anonymous Wikipedia contributor using the username "CopyleftEverything", who changed descriptions of El-Sayed's medical credentials, his association with left-wing influencer Hasan Piker and controversies involving Michigan's Jewish community.Investigative journalist Ashley Rindsberg, founder of the online campaign-influence tracker NPOV, and New York-based researcher Yehuda Teitelbaum separately examined the page's revision history and highlighted the changes on X.Rindsberg said the editor had been carrying out what appeared to be a systematic clean-up of El-Sayed's Wikipedia profile in the run-up to the election.One of the changes was made on June 12, when the wording describing El-Sayed's medical qualifications was altered. The original statement that he "has never been granted a medical license" was replaced with the softer phrase "did not pursue a medical license".El-Sayed holds a Doctor of Medicine degree from Columbia University but did not complete residency training or obtain a medical licence. During the election campaign, he faced criticism for referring to himself as a doctor.Another change involved Hasan Piker, the left-wing Twitch streamer and political commentator who appeared alongside El-Sayed at two Democratic primary-night events in April.On October 10, the description of Piker was changed from "a controversial left-wing Twitch streamer and political commentator" to "left-wing political commentator", removing the word "controversial".Piker has previously faced criticism for saying that America "deserved" the September 11, 2001, terror attacks.The researchers also flagged changes involving El-Sayed's relationship with Michigan's Jewish community. Two paragraphs, removed on October 12 and October 31, had referred to his appointment of a Jewish community liaison officer amid tensions over his criticism of the Israeli government, opposition to US military aid to Israel and remarks following the March 12 attack on Temple Israel synagogue in West Bloomfield.El-Sayed had faced criticism for saying "hurt people hurt people" while discussing the synagogue attacker's relatives, who were killed in an Israeli airstrike in Lebanon. He later apologized for the remark.The Wikipedia edits also drew a response from the platform's co-founder Larry Sanger, who described Rindsberg's findings as "old-fashioned journalism". He said the reporting was "both appropriate and effective as a criticism of Wikipedia and how it works today".Wikipedia operates on an open-editing model that allows users, including anonymous contributors, to modify articles. Changes can be made directly, although contributors are generally expected to support information with verifiable sources.Teitelbaum questioned the implications of the edits, arguing that Wikipedia's influence extends beyond the platform because Google search results and artificial intelligence systems frequently rely on its content."This is just not a random event to correct the public record," he told the New York Post. "This was really an organized effort to change the narrative in this country and to portray narratives and certain ideas that are not honest."El-Sayed defeated Republican Mike Rogers in the November 3 Michigan Senate election. His victory makes him the first Muslim American elected to the US SenateYou use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Pisces, Weekly Horoscope, November 08 to November 14, 2026: Important decisions and relationship matters shape the week
articles.summary: This week begins with a slight drag in the heart, Pisces. Monday may feel heavier than it really is, as though your mood wakes up before your hope does.
articles.body: This week begins with a slight drag in the heart, Pisces. Monday may feel heavier than it really is, as though your mood wakes up before your hope does. Work may present a few snags, and even small delays can irritate you more than usual. Drive carefully, keep your words measured, and don’t pick a fight just because your patience is thin. A little discomfort in the body, especially around the leg, can also lower your spirits. Some days are like damp mornings. You still get on with things, but the sun takes its time.The good news is that the sky clears quickly. Tuesday changes the rhythm in your favour and brings a stronger sense of success. Children do well, students feel focused, and the home atmosphere becomes easier to enjoy. Confidence returns. By Wednesday, luck seems to step in with a helping hand, especially around money and family pride. Good news from children, perhaps linked to studies, awards, or recognition, lifts your social image too. Still, your thoughts may remain somewhat unsettled even while events improve. That’s classic Pisces this week, blessings in hand, doubts still circling like late birds.Thursday and Friday deepen the positive turn. Spiritual interest rises, family support grows, and work stress reduces. Friday in particular helps smooth practical matters, while also bringing relief connected to your father’s health. Keep a careful eye on your mother’s condition though, especially if she has been neglecting rest or routine treatment. By Saturday, respect and recognition bloom in a bigger way. Society, colleagues, or relatives may speak well of you. Orders, opportunities, and praise can come together. Yet even on your best day, confusion nips at the edge. So smile, accept the good, but think twice before major commitments.Love and Relationships:Love starts the week on uneven ground, Pisces. Monday can bring friction with your spouse, and romance may feel dry or disappointing. If you’re already carrying unspoken irritation, a careless sentence could turn into a full argument. Speak softly. This is not the day to prove a point. If you are dating someone, lower expectations for dramatic closeness at the start of the week. Give each other breathing space. Sometimes affection returns faster when nobody chases it.Tuesday brings much better emotional weather. Harmony with your spouse improves, and lovers may finally get time together without interruptions or mixed signals. You’ll notice that your mood softens when everyday pressure drops. That pattern continues, though Wednesday asks for care again. There may be tension with your spouse that could leave a lasting bitter taste if handled badly. Don’t drag old history into a new disagreement. Listen first. If the issue is about family, money, or time management, solve the actual matter instead of attacking the person.From Thursday onward, the heart opens beautifully. Romance grows stronger, and your affection toward your spouse becomes more visible, more generous, more sincere. Friday adds a particularly warm touch, even in a busy schedule. You may still be occupied with work, but quality time becomes possible if you make space for it. A shared meal, a walk after dinner, or a quiet cup of tea can do wonders. Saturday keeps love in a positive zone, though your own uncertainty may make you overthink a good moment. Don’t spoil sweetness by searching for hidden problems. Let closeness be simple this weekend.Education and Career:The week opens with some friction at work. Monday may test your patience through delays, mismatched expectations, or a task that takes longer than planned. Nothing here says failure, only that you must stay steady and not react sharply. Speak carefully with colleagues, clients, and seniors. If you’re commuting for work, leave a little earlier and avoid careless driving. Students may not find Monday especially inspiring either, so use it for revision rather than trying to conquer everything at once.Tuesday brings a much stronger current for effort and achievement. Students can focus well, confidence rises, and the mind settles enough to absorb information properly. If exams, presentations, or submissions are close, this is a fine day to build momentum. Wednesday continues the positive trend in a broader way. Luck supports you, and children or younger people in the family may earn appreciation that reflects well on the household. If you work in education, management, sales, or public-facing roles, your standing improves through visible results rather than loud self-promotion.Thursday is good for business owners who want to start something new. The day carries courage and backing from family, which matters more than people admit. By Friday, your work atmosphere becomes noticeably smoother. Worries reduce. You may connect with influential people who can help your career, whether through advice, references, introductions, or future openings. Students also regain strong focus here. There may be discussion of property through your spouse’s name or family link, which could later affect your practical planning. Saturday is the brightest career day of the week. Orders may come from several sides for business people, and public respect grows. Just don’t make hurried decisions because success arrives all at once.Money and Finance:Your money story begins cautiously but improves fast, Pisces. Monday can tempt you toward speculation, and the indications are not bad, but your mood is. That matters. Don’t place money decisions in the hands of a restless mind. If you invest, do it after checking details, not while upset after an argument or rough commute. Keep spending plain and practical at the start of the week.Tuesday and Wednesday bring stronger financial luck. Speculation can work in your favour, and gains may come beyond expectation by midweek. This could be profit, a payment, a refund, a bonus, or simply money arriving from a source you had not counted on. Good news from children may also reduce future expense pressure or increase your pride in where your resources are going. There is a feeling of fortune opening a side window for you. Don’t waste that by becoming careless.Thursday is good for business people launching a fresh venture, and Friday may bring property-related benefit through your spouse’s side or name. That sounds promising, but read every paper calmly and don’t let family excitement run ahead of facts. Saturday is excellent for social standing and business orders, and once again favourable for speculation. Yet this day also carries low self-reliance and mild confusion. Strange combination, no? Money can come, praise can come, and still your judgement may wobble. So make a simple rule. No big financial move without one night of sleep and one sensible second opinion. That will save you from avoidable mistakes.Health and Well-being:Take care of your body at the start of the week, Pisces. Monday may bring slight sadness, and that emotional dip can show itself physically through tiredness, irritation, or pain in the left leg. Don’t ignore small discomfort just because the day is busy. Also, drive carefully. Your chart this week suggests that carelessness, rushing, and distraction are bigger risks than actual illness. Slow down a little. Even your speech needs handling with care, because stress can make you sharper than you intend.Tuesday brings a welcome lift. Health stays sound, your mood improves, and the body feels more cooperative. Use that better energy wisely. Catch up on sleep, eat properly, and return to a routine that supports you instead of draining you. Wednesday keeps health normal, though the mind may continue to flutter with too many thoughts. If you can, reduce noise in the evening. Less screen time, fewer unnecessary calls, and one peaceful meal can help settle your nervous system.Thursday and Friday are supportive for overall balance. Spiritual activity can be soothing, almost like cool shade in a hot afternoon. Family happiness also improves your emotional state. You may feel better simply because the people around you are easier to deal with. Friday asks you to be mindful about your mother’s health and somewhat relieved regarding your father’s improvement. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi's air quality remained in the 'very poor' category on Saturday, with an AQI of 369 as a thick layer of smog enveloped the city on the eve
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi's air quality remained in the 'very poor' category on Saturday, with an AQI of 369 as a thick layer of smog enveloped the city on the eve of Diwali, reducing visibility.The situation is likely to worsen on Sunday, with air quality expected to remain in the 'severe' category on Diwali, according to the Air Quality Early Warning System (EWS).The outlook for the subsequent six days indicates that air quality is likely to fluctuate between the 'severe' and 'very poor' categories.Of the 59 monitoring stations that recorded data, 16 reported 'severe' air quality, while 29 recorded levels in the 'very poor' category. The highest AQI of 452 was recorded near IIT Delhi.The city's average AQI improved slightly from 382 on Friday to 369 on Saturday, remaining close to the 'severe' threshold of 400. Several monitoring stations have already breached this mark, indicating a deterioration in air quality across the capital city.As per the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), an AQI between 0 and 50 is classified as 'good', 51 and 100 as 'satisfactory', 101 and 200 as 'moderate', 201 and 300 as 'poor', 301 and 400 as 'very poor', and 401 and 500 as 'severe'.Weather and air quality experts have attributed the anticipated deterioration to unfavourable meteorological conditions, the onset of Diwali-related celebrations and vehicular emissions, and the peak period of stubble burning in neighbouring states.Unfavourable weather conditions are further worsening the pollution situation. According to the EWS, a ventilation index below 6,000 square metres per second, along with an average wind speed of less than 10 kilometres per hour, hampers the effective dispersion of pollutants.PM10 was the predominant pollutant in the national capital on Saturday.According to the Decision Support System (DSS) for Delhi, the transport sector was the largest contributor to the city's pollution on Saturday, accounting for 21.4 per cent. The contribution of stubble burning was pegged at 1.7 per cent, with forecasts suggesting that it might go up to 5.4 per cent on Sunday.Satellite data detected 589 farm fire incidents across six states on Friday. Punjab accounted for the highest number at 357, followed by Madhya Pradesh (139), Rajasthan (58), Uttar Pradesh (23), Haryana (nine) and Uttarakhand (three).Between September 15 and November 6, a total of 6,226 stubble-burning incidents were recorded across the six states.The data was provided by the Consortium for Research on Agroecosystem Monitoring and Modelling from Space (CREAMS) Laboratory of the Indian Agricultural Research Institute in its bulletin.(With PTI inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: PCOS and fertility: 5 everyday lifestyle changes that may help improve ovulation and support your chances of conceiving
articles.summary: For many women, a PCOS diagnosis brings an immediate worry: Will it affect the chances of becoming a mother?
articles.body: For many women, a PCOS diagnosis brings an immediate worry: Will it affect the chances of becoming a mother? Irregular periods, hormonal changes and unpredictable ovulation can make the journey towards pregnancy confusing. But PCOS does not automatically mean infertility. Many women with the condition conceive naturally.The key lies in understanding that PCOS is not just about the ovaries. It is also linked to insulin resistance, metabolism and hormonal health. According to Dr Narendra K Shetty, Chief Wellness Officer, Kshemavana Naturopathy and Yoga Center, a combination of sensible nutrition, physical activity, adequate sleep and timely medical care can support reproductive health.Start with what goes on the plateFood choices can influence insulin levels, which matter because insulin resistance can contribute to higher androgen levels and interfere with normal ovulation.Dr Shetty recommends a balanced, largely plant-based diet containing whole grains, millets, pulses, seasonal vegetables, fruits, nuts and seeds."Particular attention should be given to including plant-based protein and fibre, choosing minimally processed grains, adding healthy fats from nuts and seeds, and cutting back on sugars, sweet drinks and highly processed foods," he explained.Instead of following restrictive diets, women can focus on sustainable eating habits that support blood sugar regulation and overall metabolic health.Move beyond exercise for weight lossPhysical activity is not simply about reducing numbers on the weighing scale. Regular movement can improve insulin sensitivity, cardiovascular health and metabolic function."Adding yoga to walking, cycling and resistance work can give extra metabolic benefits," Dr Shetty said.Practices such as Surya Namaskar, Trikonasana and Baddha Konasana can complement regular exercise, depending on individual ability. Adults can aim for 150–300 minutes of moderate-intensity physical activity each week.However, yoga should not be treated as a cure for PCOS or a guaranteed way to restore ovulation.Do not make weight the only measure of healthPCOS affects women across different body sizes. A woman with a healthy BMI can also experience insulin resistance, irregular periods and hormonal disturbances.For women carrying excess weight, gradual and sustainable weight loss may improve insulin sensitivity and menstrual regularity. But weight alone does not tell the complete story.Fitness, blood sugar control, body composition and nutritional health deserve equal attention.Give sleep and emotional health their dueFertility conversations often focus on hormones and reproductive organs, leaving emotional well-being in the background.Yet stress, poor sleep and persistent anxiety can affect overall metabolic health. Dr Shetty recommends maintaining regular sleep timings, getting seven to nine hours of rest, practising mindfulness and incorporating breathing exercises such as Nadi Shodhana and Bhramari.These practices can support well-being, although they cannot replace medical treatment.Combine lifestyle changes with timely medical carePerhaps the most important point is that natural approaches should complement, not replace, evidence-based treatment.Women experiencing prolonged gaps between periods, irregular ovulation or difficulty conceiving should seek medical evaluation. For women with anovulatory infertility due to PCOS, letrozole is a recommended first-line ovulation-induction treatment when appropriate."An integrative approach that mixes proven care with naturopathic and yogic lifestyle changes can help support overall health and reproductive well-being," Dr Shetty explained.Herbal preparations and supplements should also be discussed with a doctor, particularly when planning pregnancy.PCOS is not a verdict on motherhood. Supporting ovulation requires attention to more than menstrual cycles. Consistent lifestyle habits, metabolic health and timely medical support can help women make informed decisions about their fertility.Disclaimer: This article is for general informational purposes and is not a substitute for professional medical advice, diagnosis or treatment. Women with PCOS should consult a qualified healthcare professional before making dietary, exercise or treatment changes.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Dolly Parton's manager drops lawsuit against her nephew
articles.summary: A legal row broke out between the late singer's manager and nephew weeks after her death in August.
articles.body:
The manager of the late country music star Dolly Parton has dropped a lawsuit against her nephew.

The civil case was filed by the company that manages Parton's business interests less than a month after her death.

It included allegations of threats, intimidation and coercion against Bryan Seaver, the relative who publicly confirmed Parton had died in August. A temporary restraining order was also sought.

Seaver, who previously served as Parton's head of security, denied the allegations.

In a statement to the BBC's US partner, CBS News, Seaver's attorneys said he was "grateful to put this misunderstanding behind him so that the family can grieve peacefully".

Seaver, the son of Parton's sister Cassie, owns the security firm Squadron Augmented Protection Services (SAPS).

It provided security to Parton, who died of cancer aged 80, for the final 20 years of her life.

Weeks after Seaver confirmed her death, both he and his company were dismissed by She's Alive, which manages Parton's estate.

Danny Nozell, Parton's longtime manager and the head of She's Alive, filed for a temporary restraining order against Seaver and his company, which was granted by a judge.

In court filings, he accused Seaver of "an obscene, deliberate and escalating campaign of threats", after demanding payment from the estate.

The documents included messages in which he allegedly threatened to damage Parton's brand and business interests if his demands were not met.

The filings also alleged that Seaver used his experience as a military contractor to intimidate employees.

Seaver denied threatening the estate and in a statement published by TMZ at the time, he said he was a "career soldier and military contractor" but insisted he had simply been "talking frankly in a private way with Danny who I thought was my friend".

articles.title: Italy's Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani says 'cyber-criminals' shared his personal data on dark web
articles.summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has blamed pro-Russian hackers for publishing the details online.
articles.body:
Italy's Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani says he has been targeted by "cyber-criminals" who published his personal data online because of his country's support for Ukraine.

"For days now, cyber-criminals have been publishing my personal data on the dark web and seeking further information, effectively exposing me to new threats and intimidation," Tajani wrote on X.

He did not specify the nature of the threats, but said the hackers were also targeting his family.

The dark web is a hidden part of the internet that is not indexed by common search engines and can only be accessed with specialist software.

"Our position on Ukraine is the political reason I have been targeted," Tajani said.

"Defending the freedom of a sovereign state, taking a clear stand in support of a nation's democracy and independence, is dangerous in the eyes of these criminal entities."

Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni blamed the incident on pro-Russian hackers and offered Tajani her "full solidarity".

"The sale of confidential information about institutional representatives is a cause of serious concern and must be tackled with the utmost determination," she said in a statement.

Moscow has not publicly responded to the allegations.

Meloni also expressed concern about "circulation of false images" which she said were shared by members of Italy's opposition. She did not give details about the content of the images.

The Italian government has provided humanitarian and military support to Ukraine in its war against Russia.

Tajani, who is also the deputy prime minister, said the government was taking the threats seriously.

articles.title: A Dundee transport manager with 24 years at his company was fired after it questioned about £21,000 in pothole repair bills he had been told to arrange; a tribunal has ruled it unfair and awarded him £34,326
articles.summary: A Dundee transport manager who was dismissed after his company questioned more than £21,000 spent on pothole repairs has won £34,326 in compensation.
articles.body: A Dundee transport manager who was dismissed after his company questioned more than £21,000 spent on pothole repairs has won £34,326 in compensation. An employment tribunal ruled that Joinery and Timber Creations Ltd (JTC) had treated him unfairly and failed to conduct a proper investigation before firing him.According to STV News, S Shaw had worked for the furniture company for more than 24 years and had risen to the position of transport manager. The dispute began in 2024, when he was asked to arrange repairs to potholes in the company's factory yard in Dundee.The factory manager, Mr Freeman, had instructed Shaw to contact HB Roadways, a contractor with which JTC had a long-standing relationship. Shaw was not asked to obtain competing quotes or check the prices before arranging the work. The company's health and safety manager had previously dealt with the contractor but had since left.The issue came up during an accounts meeting in December 2024. Management questioned the amount paid to HB Roadways for the repairs and ordered an investigation. The invoices for October and November 2024 were worth £10,710 and £10,650, taking the total to £21,360.Shaw was suspended, while his line manager, Ms Patterson, investigated the matter. He was told that the company was concerned about an excessive charge for the work and whether the spending amounted to an “inappropriate use of company funds”.Investigation found no wrongdoingMs Patterson spoke to several employees as part of her investigation. She eventually concluded that Shaw had not done anything wrong. Instead, she identified “deficiencies in authorisation procedures” within the company.However, she was later removed from the investigation and did not prepare the final report. Other employees put the report together.Shaw was not told about Patterson's conclusion when he attended a disciplinary hearing with company director Mr Mulholland in January 2025. During the meeting, several allegations were raised against him. These included claims that he had denied having previous contact with HB Roadways and had deleted messages exchanged with the contractor.The tribunal heard that Shaw became extremely upset during the meeting. He told Mulholland not to come closer to him or he would “knock his block off”, or words to that effect.The judge noted that Shaw had recently experienced a family bereavement. January 22 was also the anniversary of his mother's death. He was emotional during the meeting and felt that the company was treating him badly despite his 24 years of service. JTC subsequently dismissed him. His attempts to appeal the decision were unsuccessful.Tribunal questions companyJudge Jones found serious problems with the way JTC had handled the investigation and disciplinary process. The tribunal accepted Patterson's conclusion that the company's own authorisation procedures were inadequate.It also criticised the involvement of HR manager Ms Shand in several stages of the case, including Shaw's suspension, investigation, disciplinary hearing and appeal. The tribunal described her as a “guiding hand” in the process.The company director was also unaware that the report placed before him had not been written by Patterson, who had conducted the investigation. He believed she had prepared it and did not know that her actual finding was that Shaw had done nothing wrong.As a result, Mulholland entered the disciplinary hearing without information that could have supported Shaw's case. The tribunal also described the appeal hearing as “no more than a tick box exercise”.In its ruling, the tribunal said the company had decided early on that too much money had been spent with HB Roadways and that someone had to be held responsible.It said, “A narrative was created that it must have been the claimant, and after LP had indicated that she did not believe that the claimant had done anything wrong, the respondent sought to interpret any evidence it had before it in such a way as to prove the claimant’s guilt rather than consider that evidence with an open mind.”The tribunal concluded that the decision to dismiss Shaw was “both substantively and procedurally unfair”.Company ordered to pay £34,326JTC argued that Shaw's compensation should be reduced because he would have been dismissed even if the company had followed a fair process. The tribunal rejected this argument, saying there was no evidence of misconduct or wrongdoing. It found that a proper investigation would likely have cleared him.The company also argued that Shaw's own conduct had contributed to his dismissal. However, the tribunal rejected this claim, finding that he had followed the procedures established by JTC.The tribunal ordered the company to pay him £14,350 in compensation, £500 for the loss of statutory rights and a further £19,476 as a compensatory award. The total payout was £34,326.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: South Carolina man arrested after leaving sleeping 6-year-old daughter in line for Pokémon card release, police say
articles.summary: A man was arrested in Charleston, South Carolina, on Friday after leaving his 6-year-old daughter asleep outside a Target to hold his place in line for the release of a new Pokémon trading card set, police said.
articles.body: A man was arrested in Charleston, South Carolina, on Friday after leaving his 6-year-old daughter asleep outside a Target to hold his place in line for the release of a new Pokémon trading card set, police said. Officers responded around 2:30 a.m. to the Target in Charleston’s West Ashley neighborhood after a report of an unattended child, the Charleston Police Department said in a news release. They found the girl alone. Police identified the father as John-Michael Dooley, 35, of Johns Island, South Carolina. Numerous customers had gathered outside the store overnight in anticipation of the release, according to the police. The latest expansion for the bestselling Pokémon Trading Card Game, “Mega Evolution — Delta Reign,” went on sale Friday. The decades-old Japanese franchise, which began as a children’s video game, centers on fictional creatures that players collect, train and battle. Packs starts at around $5. The release does not say whether Dooley intended to buy the cards for himself or his daughter. Witnesses told police that Dooley gave the girl a pillow and blanket before leaving her asleep in line sometime after 1 a.m. After about an hour passed without his return, concerned customers called police, authorities said. When Dooley came back to the store, witnesses identified him and he was arrested, according to the release. Police said he admitted that he had gone home and left his daughter unattended so he could keep his place in line. The child was unharmed and placed in emergency protective custody with the South Carolina Department of Social Services, police said. Dooley was charged with unlawful conduct toward a child. He is being held at the Al Cannon Detention Center, according to the release, and could not immediately be reached for comment.

articles.summary: Former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau has taken up a new role at the University of Oxford in England, joining its Blavatnik School of Government
articles.body: Former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau has taken up a new role at the University of Oxford in England, joining its Blavatnik School of Government as a Distinguished Fellow and member of the World Leaders Circle.The university announced the appointment on Friday, November 6, marking a new chapter for Trudeau after a considerable time of hiatus he took following his resignation as Canada's prime minister in 2025 following a decade in office.The World Leaders Circle is an international network of former heads of government whose experience and insights contribute to the school's work on improving governance around the world.Trudeau joins a group that includes former New Zealand Prime Minister Jacinda Ardern and former British Prime Minister Rishi Sunak."In the decade that I was prime minister, the world went through profound change both geopolitically and technologically, which fundamentally reshaped our world," Trudeau said in a statement released by Oxford.He said he looked forward to sharing his experiences, exchanging perspectives with fellow leaders and engaging with the next generation of government and policy leaders.The Blavatnik School's dean, Ngaire Woods, welcomed Trudeau's appointment, saying he brought extensive experience gained through a decade of public service. She said the initiative would provide a platform for former leaders to exchange ideas and encourage international collaboration.Trudeau is expected to visit Oxford later this month. The university said fellows would mentor students and alumni and explore new approaches to government and public policy.The appointment is among Trudeau's first major engagements since leaving political office. In September, he announced the launch of a production company, Hope & Hard Work, with his former chief of staff Katie Telford at the Toronto International Film Festival. The company plans to develop film and television projects focused on Canadian stories.Trudeau, 54, announced his intention to resign as Liberal Party leader and prime minister in January 2025 amid declining public support and growing divisions within his party.
